sourceInformation.perspective: Orthographic 2.5D; four-direction orbital defense and side-view planetary rescue
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub session protocol 1 / client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.28.2
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded geometry, dark ink outlines, paper colors and cosmic storybook scenery
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for ark, creature and engine loops; simulation-driven flight, beam and particle effects
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated synthesizer music at 10% default volume; procedural sound effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub 1–4-player ghost score chase and standalone PeerJS room codes with BroadcastChannel fallback. AI Hub and same-browser rooms tested; remote NAT traversal is unknown.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted full campaign, 18 rescues and 9 pairs; emulated standard gamepad, phone touch, offline audio analysis, developer tools, persistence, standalone two-tab rooms, and official AI Hub harness with 2/4 players, latency, jitter, loss and host departure. Native WebGPU startup and WebGL art screenshots checked.
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge, plus supplied AI Hub integration files and installed library source inspection

testingFeedback: Testing found 7 game/UI issues and 5 test-script defects. The initial 8 failed checks included cascading failures. All were corrected; the final suite contains 32 checks.
1 critical issue: the portrait phone briefing could place Launch outside the viewport, blocking touch-only launch. It now scrolls.
The input-driven browser playthrough was most helpful: it exercised real keyboard, emulated controller and touch events, then completed all three worlds with 18 rescues and 9 pairs.
Native WebGPU screenshots were least helpful because the headless canvas was blank. Game-state assertions and native WebGL fallback screenshots supplied usable evidence.
engineFeedback: Three.js node toon materials, procedural geometry and AnimationMixer made animated inked characters straightforward, while WebGPURenderer also supplied a native WebGL fallback.

I guessed wrong about short key taps surviving frame polling and about background HUD buttons belonging in menu focus. Queued actions and scoped focus fixed those assumptions. Headless WebGPU screenshots required a fallback inspection path.
The deterministic rescue and defense simulation, controller menu navigation, procedural audio, and lifecycle linking physics, menus and multiplayer.
Keeping collision state, animation, two renderer backends and multiplayer lifecycle consistent in a single self-contained file.
none; application code selects native toon materials and the provided WebGL fallback without modifying the engine.
A built-in backend-independent outline pass would simplify consistent ink rendering.
promptFeedback: The source-specific vertical slice, controller-first direction, procedural-audio constraint and concrete testing environment made the target clear.

The no-internet-research instruction coexists with a required online integration link. I treated the supplied integration files as implementation inputs and used native model knowledge for Cosmic Ark.
Completing three worlds, every input method, procedural presentation and standalone plus AI Hub multiplayer in one shareable HTML.
Bundle the AI Hub protocol files with the prompt and state explicitly whether native WebGL fallback is welcome.

aiHub.name: Cosmic Creature Cruise
aiHub.description: Defend a precious ark from four-way meteor storms, then pilot its shuttle down to three strange worlds. Beam up eighteen tiny creatures, reunite their pairs, and race your friends' ghost ships home.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD: aim or fly; Cross/Space: fire or beam; Circle/E: pulse; R2/Shift: boost; Triangle/R: early recall; Options/Esc: pause; mouse aim/fire; touch drag with assisted aim and beam.
